paper_metadata.title: Continuous Variables Quantum Algorithm for solving Ordinary Differential Equations

experiments.description: Proposed continuous-variable Koopman-von Neumann algorithm for solving a one-dimensional polynomial ordinary differential equation, with state preparation via squeezing and displacement, Trotterized gate sequence synthesis, and homodyne readout. The paper presents this as a conceptual algorithm and does not report a numerical benchmark or hardware run.

algorithm.variant: Continuous-variable Koopman-von Neumann ODE solver for 1D polynomial ODEs

hyperparameters.trotter_steps_M: sequence of integers for each order

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Vacuum state is squeezed according to required precision and then displaced by the initial value u0.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Initial condition u0 is encoded by displacing a squeezed vacuum state in the position quadrature; the ODE dynamics are encoded through the KvN Hamiltonian H_F = 1/2 (p F(q) + F(q) p).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve du/dt = F(u) for a one-dimensional polynomial F(u) and sample the evolved position distribution after time t.

problem_instance.description: Generic one-dimensional polynomial ODE; no specific coefficients, initial condition, or benchmark instance are given.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Homodyne measurement of the position quadrature and return of the sampled value.

results.unit: 2M = O(epsilon^(2/5) * t) as stated in paper

speedup_claims.factor: circumventing HHL-based exponential-in-time scaling; no explicit speedup factor quantified
speedup_claims.baseline_method: HHL-based ODE solvers / amplitude-encoded quantum ODE solvers
speedup_claims.conditions: for ODE solving via Koopman-von Neumann formalism on continuous-variable hardware
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper is conceptual and does not provide a full complexity analysis; Trotter error bounds for unbounded operators are unresolved.

speedup_claims.factor: polylogarithmic in problem size is not claimed; no explicit asymptotic advantage proven
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical ODE solvers and prior qubit-based quantum ODE solvers
speedup_claims.conditions: for the proposed CV algorithm on 1D polynomial ODEs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states that the current work does not allow for a full complexity analysis.
